4377.stem:
The graph shows Peta's heart rate, in beats per minute, during the first 60 minutes of a marathon.

\exfigure{300_q16_1}

figures.cap: graph of heart rate against time

parts.latex: What was Peta's heart rate 20 minutes after she started her marathon?
Peta started the marathon at 10 am. At what time would her heart rate first reach 140 beats/minute?

solutions.latex:
From the graph, at 20 minutes the heart rate is
$$120 \text{ beats/minute}$$

From the graph, the heart rate first reaches 140 beats/minute at 30 minutes.

Peta started at 10 am, so the time is
$$10{:}30 \text{ am}$$

meta.format_note: Added reading of 30 minutes, consistent with the 10:30 am answer.

300_q16_1.notes: Heart-rate graph with a light grey grid (10 min by 10 bpm), a zigzag break on the y-axis, and ticks every 10 with labels every 20 on y and every 10 on x. The 0.9pt smooth S-curve goes through the crop's readings (0,70), (10,90), (20,120), (30,140), (40,147) and (60,150), so the answers to (a) and (b) read the same. Round 1 started the curve at 60 by mistake; fixed in round 2. The remaining blue is the grey grid lines (scan grey compared with drawn grey). Rules 1, 3, 9, 10, 3a.

parts.latex: Which graph represents a negatively skewed distribution?

solutions.latex:
A negatively skewed distribution has a long tail on the left (the low scores), with most scores bunched towards the high end.

Option A is symmetric, B is uniform, and D has its long tail on the right (positively skewed).

Option C has its peak to the right and a long tail to the left.

So the negatively skewed graph is option C.

meta.self_check: Tail direction of each graph compared with the definition of negative skew.
meta.generated_note: Generated worked solution for MCQ; key C from option key.

271_q1_1.notes: Symmetric normal curve drawn from the Gaussian equation (rule 10) at the crop's size: peak at the crop's position, tails meeting the score axis. Plain axes with no arrowheads, as in the crop. Upright word labels 'Frequency' (rotated) and 'Score' at the crop's size. Curve 0.9pt (rule 9), axes 0.6pt. Scores just under 0.85 because the scan's normal curve is slightly uneven on the right; the redraw is symmetric on purpose (rule 10). Same frame as the other options (rule 7).

271_q1_2.notes: Uniform distribution: a horizontal line at 0.9pt from the frequency axis, with the same frame and labels as the other options (rules 7, 9).

271_q1_3.notes: Negatively skewed curve drawn as two smooth Bézier pieces fitted to the crop: long left tail, peak at the crop's position with a flat top, steep right side. Curve 0.9pt. Same frame as the other options (rules 1, 3a, 7, 9).

271_q1_4.notes: Positively skewed curve drawn as two smooth Bézier pieces fitted to the crop: steep rise, peak at the crop's position, long right tail. Curve 0.9pt. Same frame as the other options (rules 1, 3a, 7, 9). The redraw score of 0.849 is a hair under 0.85; the remaining difference is a slight shape difference along the tail.

4418.stem:
The table shows the types of customer complaints received by an online business in a month.

\extable{271_q19_t1}

parts.latex: What are the values of $A$ and $B$?

The data from the table are shown in the following Pareto chart.

\exfigure{271_q19_1}

The manager will address $80\%$ of the complaints.

Which types of complaints will the manager address?
parts.note: Reading a Pareto chart (80% rule) is no longer in the course.

criteria: Finds the correct value of $A$ or $B$

solutions.latex: The manager will address stock shortage and delivery fee.

271_q19_1.notes: Pareto chart: grey bars (98, 62, 24, 8, 6, 1), light grey gridlines every 20, left frequency axis 0–120 and right cumulative axis 0–100% with outward ticks. The cumulative line is plotted at the true values (49.2, 80.4, 92.5, 96.5, 99.5, 100%; rule 16) with dots at the bar centres. Two-line category labels, axis titles, and the rotated 'Cumulative percentage' as in the crop. The title is centred over the plot (rule 20) and kept in bold sans as printed. The chart is black and grey only. Rules 1, 2, 6, 16, 20.

parts.latex: Which histogram best represents a dataset that is positively skewed?

solutions.latex:
A positively skewed dataset has most of its scores at the low end and a long tail stretching towards the high scores on the right.

In histogram A the tallest column is on the left, and the frequencies decrease gradually towards the right, giving a long right tail.

B is the mirror image (negatively skewed), C is symmetric, and D is roughly uniform.

$$\therefore\ \text{histogram A is positively skewed}$$

meta.generated_note: MCQ working written from the answer key (A).

36_q7_1.notes: Histogram with 10 bars, positively skewed, heights measured from the crop; axes with arrowheads; 'Frequency' rotated, 'Score' below. Same frame as the other options (rule 7). Rules 1,2,3,4.

36_q7_2.notes: Negatively skewed histogram (mirror of A) in the same frame as options A and C (rule 7). 'Score' sits a few px left of the crop's because the label position is kept the same across the option set.

36_q7_3.notes: Symmetric (peaked) histogram, 10 bars, in the same frame as options A and B (rule 7). 'Score' label in the shared option-set position, a few px left of the crop's.

36_q7_4.notes: Histogram of 10 adjacent bars (roughly uniform heights) with arrowed Frequency (rotated) and Score axes, positions measured from the crop. Lines 0.6pt black, filled latex heads, label font reduced to normalsize in round 2 to match the printed size. Rules 1,2,3,4,6.

solutions.latex:
The cumulative total is a running sum of the daily downloads. It never decreases, and its steepness on each day equals that day's downloads.

The daily graph has small values at the start, peaks at about $115$ on day $10$, then falls to small values. So the cumulative graph must start near $0$, rise fastest around day $10$, then level off.

The total is about $775$, so the final bar is about $775$. For example, the sum to day $10$ is about $3+5+10+20+22+31+50+76+100+115 \approx 430$.

Options A and D start at about $80$ on day $1$, but day $1$ has only about $3$ downloads. Option B keeps speeding up and has no levelling off at the end.

Only the third graph, option C, starts low, is steepest near day $10$ (about $430$ at day $10$), and levels off at about $775$. The answer is C.

meta.self_check: Summed read-off daily values to about 775 and about 432 by day 10, matching option C.
meta.generated_note: MCQ working written from answer key; daily values read from graph.

Checker 23 Nov fix: Day moved down, clear of the day numbers.

Bars are flat grey black!30 with 1.6 px transparent gaps (rule 5: the dark scan grey lightened). Axes have filled Latex heads (rule 4), ticks every 100 on the y-axis drawn once, lines 0.6pt. 6107.stem:
The ages of members of a gardening club are shown in the stem-and-leaf plot below.

\extable{497_q15_t1}

parts.latex: How many members does the club have?
What is the median age of the members?
Describe the skewness of the distribution of ages.

solutions.latex:
Counting all the leaves in the stem-and-leaf plot gives
$$43 \text{ members}$$

With $43$ scores, the median is the $22$nd score.
$$\text{Median} = 66$$

6259.stem:
In a survey, students were asked to indicate approximately how much time they spent studying for an upcoming exam.

Students had to choose from: $0 - 1$ hours, $1 - 2$ hours, $2 - 3$ hours etc...

The graph below is the cumulative frequency ogive, which displays the results from the survey.

\exfigure{496_q22_1}

figures.cap: cumulative frequency ogive of hours spent studying

parts.latex: How many pupils were in the group?
How many pupils studied for 4 hours?
Estimate the median number of hours studied, correct to 1 decimal place.
Estimate the interquartile-range of the number of hours studied, correct to 1 decimal place.

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none). Answer read from the ogive.
Rubric written by us (source had none). Answer as given in source.
meta.corrected: Corrected from source: the answer was given in hours; the question asks how many pupils.
meta.overwritten_from_source: Corrected from source: the answer was given in hours; the question asks how many pupils.

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none).

solutions.latex:
The interquartile range is $Q_3 - Q_1$, read from the ogive.
$$\begin{aligned} IQR &= 4.3 - 2.2 \\ &= 2.1 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{approximately } 2.1 \text{ hours}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none).

496_q22_1.notes: Cumulative frequency ogive plotted at (0,0), (1,3), (2,8), (3,25), (4,28), (5,35), (6,38), (7,40), with light grey gridlines on the crop's spacing. Line and dots are black and the line is 0.9pt (rules 6, 9). The title is centred and the axis labels and outer frame are as in the crop (rule 20). The crop's typo '6.' on the x-axis is written as '6'. The redraw score is below 0.85 because the grey gridlines and serif text differ slightly from the scan's; the data line and dots match.
